record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.context_brief: p-adic lattices and permutation cocycle expansion
record.original_question: Let G be a simple p-adic Lie group of rank d at least 3, let B be the associated Bruhat-Tits building, and assume p is sufficiently large depending on d. For every lattice Γ of G, is the quotient complex Γ\B a 1-cocycle expander with permutation coefficients, i.e. does h1(Γ\B, Sym) stay positive?

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 6.1. Let G be simple p-adic Lie group of rank d ≥ 3, and p ≥ p(d) ≫ 0. Then, for any lattice Γ of G,
(6.1) h1(Γ\B , Sym) > 0,
where B is the Bruat–Tits building associated with G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple $p$-adic Lie group of rank $d \geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{B}$ denote the Bruhat–Tits building associated with $G$ (a $d$-dimensional simplicial complex on which $G$ acts). Assume $p \geq p(d)$ is sufficiently large depending on $d$. For a lattice $\Gamma \leq G$ (a discrete subgroup of finite covolume) acting on $\mathcal{B}$, form the quotient simplicial complex $\Gamma \backslash \mathcal{B}$.

For a finite simplicial complex $X$ and the system of symmetric-group coefficients $\mathrm{Sym}$ (i.e., considering 1-cochains valued in symmetric groups $S_n$, where a 1-cochain assigns to each oriented edge a permutation, and a 1-cocycle satisfies the triangle relation $f(uv)f(vw) = f(uw)$ on every 2-face), define the 1-st permutation cocycle expansion constant
$$h^1(X, \mathrm{Sym}) = \inf_n \inf_{f \in Z^1(X, S_n) \setminus B^1(X, S_n)} \frac{\mathrm{dist}(f, B^1(X, S_n))}{\|f\|},$$
where $B^1$ denotes the set of 1-coboundaries and the distance and norm are normalized Hamming distances on edges (after minimizing over conjugation by 0-cochains).

Question: Is it the case that for every such lattice $\Gamma$ in $G$,
$$h^1(\Gamma \backslash \mathcal{B}, \mathrm{Sym}) > 0?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is formulated as a conjecture in the literature on stability of homomorphisms and high-dimensional expanders. Related cosystolic expansion conjectures for quotients of high-rank Bruhat–Tits buildings (with non-abelian/permutation coefficients) are described as open in recent surveys and papers on Ramanujan complexes and HDX. No resolution was found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: High Dimensional Expanders — Lubotzky
status_evidence.snippet: It is natural to conjecture that the Ramanujan complexes and more generally the quotients of the high rank Bruhat-Tits buildings ... are still cosystolic expanders. But this is open.
status_evidence.claim: Cosystolic/cocycle expansion of quotients of high-rank Bruhat–Tits buildings is described as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: High-dimensional expanders from Kac–Moody–Steinberg groups
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of high-dimensional expanders related to Bruhat–Tits-type buildings, with open questions about non-abelian cocycle expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats cocycle expansion with non-abelian coefficients as an active open direction.
